method: Independent full reading of the five assigned outgoing bodies and editorial notes in emma.packet.json, followed by targeted comparison with receipt/order cues in the surviving Emma correspondence. XML sent-date constraints are preserved verbatim; section dates are proposed only where the body or editorial note supplies them.

outgoing_reviews.uncertainty: Retain the full 12–24 October range. The editorial 19 October weighing note is a contextual visit record, not a whole-letter composition date.
outgoing_reviews.related_incoming_order: Paragraph 1 reports old letters shown by Nancy and Aunt Bessy, while paragraph 3 says Darwin is looking over Emma's letter; these are references/events, not sufficient to establish a separately dated incoming Emma letter for this body.

findings: 448 is the only assigned record where the XML @when single day is contradicted by the display range and an explicit body section dateline; paragraphs 1–6 are Friday 30 November and paragraph 7 is Saturday 1 December.
466, 481 and 484 contain later explicit section datelines. Their earliest XML bounds must not be propagated to later or earlier sections without the body cue.
704 remains a broad bounded range; internal relative dates and the editorial weighing note do not establish one exact composition date.
Incoming-letter receipt cues were kept separate from calendar dating and from claims that an incoming letter was available to earlier paragraphs.
limitations: This is a section-date review, not a reply graph or transcription audit. It does not alter the canonical metadata audit or any correspondent review.
verdict: Preserve all five XML date constraints. Promote only explicit internal section datelines to exact paragraph-level dates; retain candidate or unresolved status for sections supported only by bounds, relative cues, or editorial contextual notes.
